Usage: gotools install [options] [name] <pkg>

  Install a Go tool via 'go get -tool'. If only a package is given, the tool
  name is inferred from the package path.

  Tool aliases: you can give the tool a custom name (alias). The alias is used
  in gotools (list, info, remove, exec, upgrade) but the underlying Go binary
  name stays the same.

  If the package is already managed under a different name, install asks how to
  proceed: 1) install another entry under the new name, 2) upgrade the existing
  entry to the requested version, 3) rename the existing entry to the new name,
  or 4) skip (nothing changes). On non-interactive stdin it prints the situation
  and installs under the requested name.

  Pipe mode: feed 'go install' commands via stdin. The 'go install' prefix is
  optional, so a bare pkg@version works too.

    echo 'go install pkg@latest' | gotools       # pipe
    gotools <<< 'go install pkg@latest'          # herestring
    gotools <<EOF                                # heredoc
    go install pkg1@v1
    go install pkg2@v2
    EOF
    gotools < tools.txt                          # file redirect

  Examples:
    gotools install golang.org/x/tools/cmd/goimports@latest
    gotools install mylint golang.org/x/tools/cmd/goimports@v0.38.0
    gotools exec mylint -w .   # runs the goimports binary

  Options:
    --force    Overwrite an existing tool with the same name
    --offline  Refuse to install (needs the network), exit 6
